reproduction_target: Image-analysis and spatial-omics computational pipeline of the MERFISH+ human developing heart study: probe library design (LibraryDesigner, NSForest v2 panel selection), MERFISH image pre-processing / spot localization / barcode decoding (MERlin v0.6.1 and a modified MERlin for the 3D dataset), Cellpose v2 cell and nuclear segmentation, transcript-to-cell assignment, Leiden clustering and manual cell-type curation, Spateo-based 53-slice rigid alignment and 3D reconstruction, Spateo/PyVista 3D visualization, downstream spatial statistics (kNN density, co-existence dendrogram, neighborhood enrichment, DBSCAN vessel-network construction, mesh-based layer thickness, expression-gradient analysis), pseudo-bulk correlation, the Spateo-VI / MERFISHVI variational model, and chromatin-tracing trace computation plus protein density quantification. Wet-lab work (tissue procurement and sectioning, probe synthesis, hydrogel embedding/clearing, hybridization and microfluidics, antibody staining, chromatin-tracing hybridization, image acquisition, pipetting-robot operation) is out of computational-reproduction scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis-invocation extracted from the STAR Methods 'DATA ANALYSIS' block plus the probe-design and chromatin-tracing analysis subsections. Cellpose v2 segmentation for the 3D dataset is folded into the 2D Cellpose step where the paper states 'the same method as above'. Sub-steps of the 3D-thickness workflow are kept separate because the paper gives them distinct parameterized procedures (surface construction, IVS identification, thickness computation). Wet-lab procedures counted in W, not verdicted. No line-by-line code reading was performed (stage-1 prose triage only); the listed repositories were checked for HTTP liveness and README prose only.

steps.label: Primary probe library design (1835-gene panel) with the Python workflow at github.com/deprekate/LibraryDesigner: 17-mer index from hs1 assembly (DNA) / hg38 transcriptome (RNA), 40-mer candidates, 5-60 probes per gene, filtering on GC, Tm, repeat masking, off-target 17-mer counts
MERFISH gene-panel marker selection with NSForest v2, default parameters, on the previously published 12-15 p.c.w. heart scRNA-seq dataset (ref 15), supplemented with literature markers

Chromatin (DNA) probe design for the FXYD7 locus: 10-kb partitioning, screening against hs1/hg38 with the same 17-mer off-target pipeline (coords chr19:35003250-35533250 hg38 / chr19:37547865-38078198 hs1)
Analysis of 2D heart sections imaged with acrydite-modified MERFISH probes using MERlin v0.6.1 'exactly as previously described' (ref 15)
Cell-type assignment and UMAP generation with the Scanpy 'ingest' function, mapping newly generated data onto previously published MERFISH data (ref 93)

MERFISH+ image pre-processing with custom scripts: per-colour flat-field correction by per-pixel median of round 1, Wiener deconvolution with a microscope-specific measured PSF, high-pass filter blur sigma = 30
Fluorescent spot localization: local maxima within 1-pixel radius, filtered to brightness >= 3600 and PSF correlation >= 0.25
smFISH transcript quantification: spots further filtered on minimum brightness relative to local background, threshold selected per colour channel and 'manually tuned'

MERFISH+ decoding: drift-corrected clustering of spots within 2 pixels, hamming-weight-4 codebook with >= 3 spots kept (single-bit-error correction), L2-normalized brightness vector matched to codebook, three-metric Fisher-combined score with threshold chosen to separate blank vs gene score distributions
3D cell segmentation with Cellpose v2: per-z-slice 2D masks from the flat-field-corrected and deconvolved DAPI channel using the 'dapi' model, then linking across adjacent z-slices
Assignment of smFISH and MERFISH transcripts to cells: coordinates adjusted by computed inter-image drift, rounded to nearest integer, assigned by segmentation-mask value

3D-heart RNA molecule localization with a modified MERlin v0.6.1 (compressed Zarr support, DAPI-based drift correction including z-axis, FFT anchor-point offsets, high-pass + Gaussian-PSF deconvolution, pixel-wise L2-normalized barcode matching with distance < 0.6, iterative scale-factor estimation over 50 random z-slices x 10 iterations, 3D-histogram filtering to a 5% misidentification rate)

Cell clustering and curation: Leiden clustering, manual major-cell-type labelling, merging, per-type sub-clustering with manual labelling, artifact-cluster identification, nearest-neighbour imputation of cell type for 72,142 (2.3%) out-of-focus-affected cells using unaffected genes, removal of low-quality clusters

Slice alignment and 3D reconstruction of 53 coronal slices with Spateo morpho_align in rigid mode; Scanpy-computed PCA features as input; partial_robust_level = 25 for partially overlapping sections (e.g. 21/22); defaults elsewhere; run on Ubuntu 22.04.5, Intel Xeon Platinum 8280, 1.4 TB RAM, 8x NVIDIA A100 40 GB, ~1 h runtime
3D visualization with Spateo's PyVista-based renderer: construct_pc to convert h5ad to VTK, add_model_labels for scalar fields, opacity rescaled to 0-1, three_d_plot for rendering
Per-cell-type k-nearest-neighbour density: distance d to the k-th nearest same-type neighbour (k = 30), density = same-type cells within radius d divided by (4/3)pi r^3

Cell-type co-existence neighbourhood analysis (Figures 5A/5B): NxM neighbourhood composition matrix, pairwise Pearson co-existence scores, scipy pdist with 'cityblock' metric, scipy linkage with 'single' method for the dendrogram, igraph network visualization with edges below score 0.07 filtered out, five niche neighbourhoods annotated manually

Neighbourhood cell-type enrichment along coronary branches (Figure 5H): cellular composition within a 30 um radius of the LAD, LCX and RCA branches, normalized against whole-heart background cell-type frequencies

Coronary artery vessel-network construction (Figure 5E): top 3% MYH11-expressing cells as candidate vessel cells, AO/PA cells excluded spatially, three iterations of density filtering (lowest 10%, 3%, 0.5%), DBSCAN from scikit-learn with eps = 50 um and min_samples = 5 (noise label -1 excluded), top-down tree construction with angular + Euclidean connection loss weighted by w = 0.5, predefined manual connections where the top-down relation fails

Layer surface mesh construction (Figures 4H-4K): per-layer point clouds from defined cell types, iterative removal of lowest 1% density cells, Spateo st.tdr.construct_surface with marching cubes, mc_scale_factor = 1.05, dist_sample_num = 1000, levelset = 0.4, z-axis compressed 5x during meshing and rescaled afterwards; epicardial, endocardial and hybrid layers reconstructed

Interventricular septum (IVS) region identification (Figure 4H): per-vertex normal-vector intersection tests between left/right endocardial meshes and the epicardial mesh, with five-case classification (cases 1-3 labelled IVS, cases 4-5 assigned to right/left walls)

3D physical layer-thickness computation (Figures 4H-4K, S8): per-epicardial-vertex normal intersections with endocardial, hybrid and Purkinje meshes; trabecular / hybrid / compact / free-wall thicknesses defined from consecutive intersection distances
Gene-expression gradient analysis along the vascular hierarchy (Figures 5I-5K): path from each vascular cell to its vessel root, then path-dependent differential expression

Correlation of RNA expression measurements: pseudo-bulk Pearson correlations on log10(x+1)-transformed mean transcript counts per gene from raw cell-by-gene tables; cell-type-vs-cell-type heatmaps from per-gene z-scored means; overall correlation summarized as the mean of per-cell-type maximum correlations

Spateo-VI / MERFISHVI integration model (Figure 6): spatial graph via KNN (default 10 neighbours, symmetrized) or Delaunay triangulation (spatial_graph_type parameter), multi-head GATv2 attention encoder producing a Gaussian spatial latent (epsilon = 1e-4), scVI-style VAE with MLP encoder (n_layers / n_hidden), negative-binomial (or ZINB) decoder with gene-specific overdispersion

Chromatin tracing analysis: FFT-based image registration across hybridization rounds using DAPI local maxima/minima, nuclear segmentation with the Cellpose 'nuclei' neural-network model, chromatin traces computed from drift-corrected per-locus local maxima 'as previously described' (ref 40)

Protein density quantification on chromatin traces: antibody images flat-field corrected, deconvolved, registered to the chromatin traces via DAPI; per-trace antibody signal sampled at each genomic-locus 3D position in each cell

headline.static_readiness: 0/27 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: Under an inference-inclusive reading the ceiling is 1 RI / 27 (C2, NSForest v2 with default parameters on a previously published scRNA-seq dataset). Every other computational step consumes the newly generated MERFISH+ / chromatin-tracing imaging data, for which the paper provides NO data-availability statement and NO repository accession - only 'available from the lead contact upon request' - so the data axis is 0 and each step caps at NI regardless of code quality. Code repositories are listed (six GitHub URLs) but with no commit, tag, release or archive DOI, and one of them (aristoteleo/MERFISHVI, the Spateo-VI model) returns HTTP 404. Version pins are partial and coarse (MERlin v0.6.1, Cellpose v2, NSForest v2, Ubuntu 22.04.5); Spateo, Scanpy, scipy, scikit-learn, igraph, PyVista and LibraryDesigner are unpinned. No lockfile, conda environment or container is claimed anywhere.
headline.coverage: 27 computational steps assessed from STAR Methods prose (DATA ANALYSIS block plus probe-design and chromatin-tracing analysis subsections); 8 wet-lab steps counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope. A Code availability statement is present in two places; no Data availability statement or dataset accession exists anywhere in the paper.

gaps.where: All MERFISH+ / smFISH / chromatin-tracing imaging data and the derived cell-by-gene tables (C4-C27)
gaps.missing: No Data availability statement and no accession of any kind (GEO / SRA / ENA / ArrayExpress / dbGaP / EGA / figshare / Zenodo / Dryad / BioStudies / BioImage Archive) appears anywhere in the manuscript. The only statement is 'Any additional information required to reanalyze the data reported in this paper is available from the lead contact upon request.' A browsing portal (https://zhu.merfisheyes.com/) exists but is a viewer, not a deposited, citable dataset.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the raw or minimally processed image data (e.g. BioImage Archive / Zenodo) and the decoded cell-by-gene matrices, segmentation masks, cell-type labels and the aligned 3D coordinates (h5ad) under citable accessions, and add an explicit Data availability statement.

gaps.where: Software environment for the entire analysis stack (C1, C3-C27)
gaps.missing: No conda environment, requirements file, lockfile or container image is claimed in the paper or in the repository landing pages inspected. Version information is partial and coarse: MERlin v0.6.1, Cellpose 'v2', NSForest v2, and an OS string (Ubuntu 22.04.5) with hardware description. Spateo, Scanpy, scipy, scikit-learn, igraph, PyVista, LibraryDesigner and the Spateo-VI/MERFISHVI model are entirely unversioned. Hardware description (Xeon 8280, 8x A100) is not an environment capture.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a resolved environment (conda-lock / pixi.lock / uv.lock) or a container image referenced by digest, covering the MERlin fork, Cellpose, Spateo, Scanpy and the scientific-Python stack; state the exact Cellpose minor version rather than 'v2'.

gaps.where: Code availability statement (all six repository URLs)
gaps.missing: Repositories are given as bare GitHub URLs with no commit SHA, tag, release or archival DOI (Zenodo/Software Heritage). The listed https://github.com/aristoteleo/MERFISHVI returns HTTP 404 at assessment time, so the code for the Spateo-VI model described in Figure 6 is not retrievable. The modified MERlin fork used for the 3D dataset (Zarr support, DAPI-based z-drift correction) is described in prose but no fork/branch is identified among the listed URLs. github.com/epigen-UCSD/MERFISH_Plus_Paper resolves but exposes no README prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Archive each repository at the exact analysis state (Zenodo DOI or commit SHA) and cite those pins; publish or fix the MERFISHVI repository; explicitly identify the MERlin fork/branch used for the 3D reconstruction.

gaps.where: C6-C9, C11, C13, C15-C24, C26-C27 (custom MERFISH+ and downstream spatial-analysis steps)
gaps.missing: The prose describes bespoke algorithms in detail but does not tie any individual step to a named script, notebook, entry point or command line in the listed repositories. There is no stated run order, no configuration files, and no codebook file for the MERFISH decoding.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide a driver script or workflow (Snakemake/Nextflow/notebook series) with a documented entry point per figure panel, plus the MERFISH codebook, the measured PSF, and the cell-type label tables as versioned inputs.

gaps.where: C8 (smFISH threshold), C9 (decoding score threshold), C13 (Leiden resolution and artifact-cluster criteria), C23 (differential-expression method)
gaps.missing: Several decisive thresholds are described as 'manually tuned' or 'chosen to separate the peaks' without numeric values; the Leiden resolution parameter and the criteria for calling clusters 'artifacts' are not given; the path-dependent differential-expression test in C23 is not named.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the numeric per-channel smFISH thresholds and the final decoding score cutoff, the Leiden resolution and neighbour-graph settings, the explicit artifact-cluster criteria, and the statistical test and correction used for the gradient analysis.

gaps.where: C13 (manual cell-type labelling and merging), C17 (manual niche annotation), C19 (predefined manual vessel connections), C20 (manual left-right cell separation), C18 (manual coronary-branch definition)
gaps.missing: Multiple steps involve human curation whose outputs are not deposited: the manual major/sub cell-type label assignments, the five manually annotated niche neighbourhoods, the ad hoc manual vessel-tree connections, and manual left/right splits during mesh construction. Without these curated artifacts the pipeline is not deterministically re-runnable.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the curated label tables, the annotated dendrogram groupings, and the explicit list of manually added vessel-tree edges as machine-readable files.

gaps.where: C1, C3 (probe design references) and C12 (barcode codebook)
gaps.missing: Reference resources are named at assembly level only (hs1 assembly, hg38 transcriptome) with no accession, patch level, source URL or download date; the MERFISH codebook used for decoding is not provided.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the reference genome/transcriptome releases (accession + release date + source URL) and deposit the codebook and final probe sequence set.

gaps.where: Wet-lab: tissue procurement and coronal sectioning under IRB 172111 / 101021, MERFISH+ acrydite probe synthesis and purification, hydrogel embedding and tissue clearing, hybridization rounds on the custom microfluidics system, epigenetic-marker antibody staining, chromatin-tracing hybridization, imaging acquisition (20 Hz, 4 colours, 300 nm z-steps over 15 um), pipetting-robot operation
gaps.missing: Wet-lab generation and validation steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W, not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; scope is the image-analysis and spatial-omics pipeline.

gaps.missing: Samples are human fetal heart tissue collected under UCSD IRB-approved protocols with donor-family consent. Even if imaging data were deposited, access may be subject to human-subjects restrictions that the paper does not describe.
gaps.how_to_close: State the intended access regime for the human-derived data (open vs controlled) and, if controlled, register it under a managed-access repository with a documented application route.
